detail.abstract: Problem definition: Personalized screening is typically a dynamic decision that accounts for a patient's disease risk, prior clinical history, and screening costs. However, screening decisions optimal at the individual level may not be jointly implementable when limited screening resources are shared across multiple patients. In this study, we investigate how a policy maker should coordinate personalized screening decisions across patients, screening methods, and time when disease states are only partially observable and screening capacity is constrained. Methodology/results: We formulate the problem as a finite-horizon weakly coupled partially observable Markov decision process that captures patient-level disease and information dynamics together with population-level screening capacity constraints. We use the Lagrangian relaxation approach to decompose the joint optimization problem into patient-level dynamic screening problems, and propose a scalable index-based policy that produces capacity-feasible assignments across patients and screening methods. As a performance guarantee, we show that the index policy is asymptotically optimal when the population size and screening capacities scale proportionally. Such theoretical convergence property is validated through controlled numerical studies. We further apply our framework to a case study for mammography screening with heterogeneous patients and constrained capacity. Using calibrated parameters, we show that the index policy achieves higher expected quality-adjusted life years than commonly used heuristic policies in practice. Managerial implications: Our results highlight the importance of coordinating personalized screening decisions at the population level when patients' health states are partially observed and screening resources are shared. They are practically relevant to public healthcare policy makers managing screening decisions for a large population, especially in less developed regions with limited screening resources.

detail.abstract: Behavioural health outcomes are shaped by interacting psychological, social, economic, environmental and service-system factors. Public health agencies increasingly hold data that could help identify population-level needs, detect changes in risk, evaluate interventions and allocate resources. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and natural language processing, can support the integration and analysis of these heterogeneous data; however, predictive performance alone does not establish that an output is valid, equitable or useful for public policy. This conceptual review examines how AI-driven behavioural health analytics may contribute to evidence-based public health policy formulation and proposes a governance-centred framework linking data stewardship, analytical modelling, evidence synthesis, deliberation, implementation and evaluation. The discussion draws on established literature concerning digital phenotyping, mental health prediction, algorithmic bias, public health surveillance and responsible AI governance. It distinguishes potential applications from demonstrated policy impact and highlights persistent limitations: non-representative data, weak external validation, construct ambiguity, privacy risks, opaque models, digital exclusion and the difficulty of translating individual-level predictions into population-level decisions. The proposed framework treats AI as decision support rather than an autonomous policy-maker and places community participation, transparent uncertainty communication, independent evaluation and ongoing monitoring at each stage. For policy teams, the central implication is that AI analytics should complement not replace epidemiological evidence, qualitative community knowledge and democratic accountability. Future studies should evaluate not only predictive accuracy but also policy relevance, distributional effects, implementation feasibility and measurable population outcomes.

detail.abstract:
Physical AI technologies, humanoid robots among them, are expected to reach commercial use first in manufacturing, where interaction with people is comparatively limited. Raising the competitiveness of manufacturing through autonomous production, in which human intervention is minimized, will require a manufacturing artificial intelligence (AI) transformation (AX) built on physical AI and capable of handling the wide range of unstructured tasks a factory presents. Viewed from that standpoint, the physical AI ecosystem has six core elements: form factor development and design, manufacturing-specific AI behavior learning, actuators, robot hands, AI foundation models, and on-device AI semiconductors.

South Korea holds a comparative advantage in manufacturing-specific AI behavior learning, and this study proposes a K-Physical AI Ecosystem Expansion Strategy that uses that advantage as a bridgehead for widening Korea’s presence across the ecosystem. Reaching the goal of joining the global top three in AI robots, set out in the Three Megaprojects for a Great Leap Forward for South Korea, depends on accumulating manufacturing-specific behavior learning and data built on a Korean physical AI robot form factor of the country’s own. What is also needed is a manufacturing AX roadmap by industry and process, one that widens the scope of application in stages, moving from AI robots for light work to general-purpose and then heavy-duty applications as physical AI technology matures and conditions on the factory floor allow. For the physical AI transition in Korea’s flagship manufacturing industries, policy should be pursued at the level of the industry and the industrial complex, matched to the form of AI robot that each industry and process requires.

detail.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine technology is a transformative platform for rapid vaccine development. To address inequitable access, the WHO and Medicines Patent Pool (MPP) established the mRNA Technology Transfer Program, with Afrigen as development hub and Biovac as the first manufacturing partner. Following successful 1 L technology demonstration at Biovac, process optimization was performed to improve yield, efficiency, and cost while maintaining compliance with predefined critical quality attributes. Key changes included removal of intermediate tangential flow filtration steps, reduced diafiltration volumes, improved IVT yield, and reduced capping enzyme usage. Two optimized drug substance (DS) confirmation batches were manufactured at the 0.4 L IVT scale selected to generate mRNA mass equivalent to the original 1 L process while remaining within chromatography loading constraints. IVT yields were 7.20–7.61 mg/mL, chromatography recovery was 85%, and TFF recoveries were 92–94%. Final DS masses were 2.44 g and 2.67 g, corresponding to overall recoveries of 73 –77%, exceeding the 1 L technical demonstration batch (1.99 g; 64% recovery). One DS batch was further processed into drug product (DP) at the 5.5 L encapsulation scale (scale volume based on the total encapsulation output namely: diluted mRNA, lipid mix and formulation buffer), and all DP critical quality attributes met predefined specifications. These results confirm successful implementation of the optimized DS process and demonstrate its capability to produce compliant DS and DP with improved yield and recovery.

detail.abstract: Accurate lodging demand forecasting and proactive pricing decisions are essential for modern hospitality revenue management. This study presents a predictive analytics framework using the Hotel Booking Demand dataset across Resort and City properties. Daily net bookings (D t) are aggregated during data preprocessing and subsequently decomposed via STL time series analysis into trend, seasonal, and remainder components. Comparative forecasting architectures SARIMA, XGBoost, and LSTM neural networks are evaluated across a 90-day testing horizon. In our experimental model evaluation, XGBoost achieved a simulated benchmark MAPE of 3.82% and RMSE of 5.14, outperforming LSTM (4.58%) and SARIMA (8.41%). Feature importance analysis identifies booking lead time and Average Daily Rate (ADR) as primary demand drivers. Integrating XGBoost predictions into a dynamic revenue management simulation yielded an estimated 14.8% revenue lift, while low-demand pricing rules increased simulated occupancy from 52% to 64%. These results illustrate the potential operational value of combining gradient boosted decision trees with dynamic yield management in property management systems.

detail.abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court has pushed the United States into a new system of public governance, “Presidentialism,” which gives unprecedented economic regulatory power and enforcement power to the President. Compensation arrangements designed to align shareholder and managerial interests now give the President additional power to obtain corporate compliance with preferred policy positions because of the concentrated firm-specific pecuniary stakes of managers and directors. In the name of protecting the democracy against authoritarian over-reach, we need new corporate governance institutions that insulate decision-makers from this pecuniary pressure, here, a Public Integrity Committee at the board level, compensated without stock and protected through staggered terms. Similarly, the exposure of asset managers to pressure over their stewardship voting strategies call for divestment of voting authority to decentralized but autonomous voting offices. This preserves the efficiency of centralized fund administration and portfolio assembly and marketing while divesting the asset manager of voting authority that makes it a potential target of Presidentialist pressure.

detail.abstract:
The Supreme Court has long recognized the parent-child relationship as a fundamental liberty interest but has never supplied a determinate constitutional floor governing its infringement. That omission has consequences. As sex-based parental priority rules gave way to equal protection, disputes between fit parents increasingly required decisions by courts and court-adjacent professionals operating under indeterminate best-interests standards. Adjudicative authority migrated toward evaluators, therapists, parenting coordinators, and private arbitrators, often without the constitutional safeguards associated with the exercise of state power.

This amicus brief, filed in support of the petition for certiorari in Loop v. Washington, No. 26-369, addresses whether a State may enforce a private arbitrator's determination substantially burdening a fit parent's relationship with a child without constitutionally adequate adjudication. Drawing on the Supreme Court's precedents concerning parental liberty, procedural due process, neutral decision-makers, heightened evidentiary burdens, state action, and equal protection, the brief argues that private delegation cannot relieve the State of its constitutional obligations.

The brief also identifies a broader, administrable constitutional construction assembled from existing principles: protection of each fit parent-child relationship; bounded state protective power with an immediate emergency safety lane; seven stabilizing rules governing intervention, evidence, judicial accountability, cooperation, and reversibility; and independent First Amendment protections for conscience, speech, and petition. This proposed floor would constrain state interference without federalizing custody schedules or prescribing a single model of family life.

The brief does not ask the Court to adopt the complete construction at the certiorari stage. Rather, it demonstrates that the constitutional question presented is recurring, consequential, and capable of a principled resolution. It urges the Court to grant review.

detail.abstract: Background: Efficient hospital supply-chain management is essential for maintaining the availability of medical supplies and equipment. Conventional minimum-stock thresholds may not adequately reflect inventory status when consumption and replenishment lead time are considered. This study compared minimum-stock adequacy with estimated lead-time-adjusted inventory coverage and examined associated item, vendor, and financial characteristics.,Method: A secondary observational analysis was conducted using 500 dated inventory records from a publicly available hospital supply-chain dataset. Below-minimum inventory and estimated insufficient lead-time coverage were evaluated as complementary outcomes. Descriptive and bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed, accompanied by regression diagnostics, internal validation, and sensitivity analyses for inventory-capacity inconsistencies. Vendor characteristics and date-linked expenditure were also assessed.,Results: Among 500 inventory records, 43 (8.6%; 95% CI: 6.45–11.38%) were below the recorded minimum stock level, whereas 299 (59.8%; 95% CI: 55.44–64.01%) met the criterion for estimated insufficient lead-time coverage. Median stock coverage was 9.31 days (IQR: 5.45–17.68), compared with a median restock lead time of 16 days. Notably, 262 of 457 (57.33%) records at or above the minimum threshold still had estimated insufficient coverage. No strong independent associations were identified for the examined item, vendor, or financial characteristics. Model discrimination was weak, with the below-minimum model yielding an apparent AUC of 0.582 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.519. Capacity-restricted sensitivity analyses showed that the principal coverage pattern persisted.,Conclusion: Minimum-stock status and estimated lead-time-adjusted coverage identified substantially different patterns of inventory adequacy. Lead-time-adjusted coverage may complement conventional minimum-stock assessment but should be interpreted as a derived indicator rather than evidence of observed stockout. Validation using longitudinal, transaction-level hospital data is required before operational application.

detail.abstract: Vaccine research and development (R&D) priority setting is highly context-dependent, with numerous lists developed internationally to meet different objectives. Canada’s unique epidemiology and social context shape its public health needs, necessitating the tailored approach reflected in the 2025 Vaccine R&D Report. This set of vaccine R&D priorities, focused on human health, was developed using a multi-stage process, relying on consultation across Canada with individuals with expertise in infectious diseases, public health, surveillance, epidemiology, and vaccine research. Pathogens were identified and ranked based on weighted, pathogen-specific evidence, with final consensus achieved through a modified Delphi process. The combined use of a multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) and a modified Delphi process effectively generated a robust and defensible pathogen priority list to guide future vaccine R&D efforts in Canada.

detail.abstract: We provide a uniform guarantee for a continuous-review lost-sales inventory system with unit Poisson demand, deterministic lead time, and fixed ordering costs: a simple algorithm computes an (r, Q) policy and chooses between that policy and no replenishment, with cost at most (√ 2 + √ 6)/2 < 1.932 times the unrestricted nonanticipative optimum. The algorithm starts by generating an optimal integer base-stock policy, which at zero setup cost achieves the tight worst-case factor √ 2 relative to the optimal system cost. For positive setup costs, it uses the reorder point of this integer base-stock policy and an integer lot at the economic order quantity scale. The inclusion of ordinary base stock in the continuous-review capped base-stock family also improves that family's earlier asymptotic 1.79 upper guarantee to a uniform √ 2 guarantee valid at every finite parameter vector. To establish these guarantees, we construct a computable lower bound on the zero-setup optimal cost by tracking units already on hand or committed for delivery. We then combine it with a bound on holding and setup costs required by batching to obtain the general-setup guarantee and instance-specific performance bounds for any admissible replenishment policy. In our numerical study, the largest estimated policy-cost-to-lower-bound ratios are about 1.59 for our heuristic (r, Q) policy and 1.47 after joint optimization of r and Q. The heuristic also performs well against the optimized policy: over the sampled instances, its median extra cost ranges from 2.33% to 3.91%, depending on the setup cost.

detail.abstract:
This Article conceptualizes China as a "platform state" that governs innovation by orchestrating an ecosystem composed largely of relatively autonomous yet highly interdependent firms. This model of governance follows three strategic principles that resembles those of a platform company: prioritizing ecosystem orchestration over picking winners, embedding control in key interfaces alongside selective ownership, and scaling first and capturing value later. 

Although China is neither the first nor the only country to adopt a platform strategy to spur innovation, it stands apart in combining strong state capacity with the vast domestic base needed to scale innovation. As state intervention relies less on ownership and hierarchical command, governance within the platform state becomes more rule-bound. During the growth stage, law primarily performs enabling functions: signaling policy endorsement, distributing subsidies and other resources to attract participation, authorizing experimentation to facilitate deployment, and coordinating standard setting and infrastructure development. As the ecosystem matures, law assumes a more prominent ordering role: adjudicating disputes among participants, regulating their interactions and exit, disciplining misconduct that threatens the state's strategic interests, and constraining bureaucratic discretion to curb rent seeking. Law thus forms a central part of the institutional architecture through which the state builds and governs its innovation ecosystem. 

The platform-state model helps explain how entrepreneurial dynamism can coexist with extensive and growing state influence, how state capacity can expand even when private returns remain weak, and why the Chinese state may constrain the very firms it has helped grow. This model also generates a state-capacity flywheel that strengthens Beijing's ability to scale innovation from one technological frontier to the next. By shifting the unit of analysis from individual firms to the innovation ecosystem as a whole, the platform-state framework advances a new organizational theory of state capitalism and broadens the conventional scope of industrial policy. It also offers a more nuanced and balanced account of Chinese institutions and contributes to a richer understanding of the functions of law in China.

detail.abstract: Autonomous and assisted driving have turned the automotive system-on-chip (SoC) into one of the most strategic components in a vehicle. This paper examines the market for autonomous-driving chips as of October 2026. It asks three questions: how growth in onboard AI workloads has reshaped demand for compute; how market structure is evolving between merchant suppliers and automaker in-house designs; and which constraints govern chip choice. Using company filings, industry installation data and secondary sources, we document a roughly hundredfold increase in fitted compute for comparable driving functions since about 2020. This increase is driven by end-to-end and vision-language-action (VLA) models with billions of parameters. In China, the largest market for advanced assisted driving, NVIDIA's share of domain-controller chip installations fell from 45.1% to 30.2% between early and August 2026, while Horizon Robotics rose from 9.3% to 19.8%. Leading Chinese automakers now ship their own 5nm and 4nm designs. A case study of NIO's Shenji NX9031 illustrates the economics of vertical integration: high fixed costs offset by per-vehicle savings and, increasingly, by external licensing. We interpret these developments through transaction-cost, property-rights and appropriability theory, and derive five propositions on when automakers make rather than buy driving chips. Chip choice is jointly constrained by cost, energy draw from the traction battery (5-15% of EV range), and new cybersecurity regulations (UN R155/R156; China's GB 44495-2024). We also map process nodes (from 8nm down to 2nm-class) and foundries, review US and Chinese export-control measures, describe the digital-twin and hardware-in-the-loop methods used to validate chips before installation, and compare published performance across five architecture types and seven L4 robotaxi operators, showing that peak TOPS is a weak predictor of real-world L4 safety. Finally, we map the upstream and downstream value chain, including optical data links and satellite positioning, where gross margins follow a smile curve: about 47-75% in chip design, against about 16-18% in integration and operations. We discuss implications for automakers, chip suppliers and policymakers.

detail.abstract: Claims that human endorsement legitimises failed automation need evidence connecting an act of authorisation to the process it is said to legitimate. This comparison of England's Ofqual grading arrangements and Australia's Robodebt scheme tests those connections in Someyo Kamal Utsho's account, building on existing pairedcase and Robodebt scholarship. Ofqual reports model evaluation and student-level outcome analysis, but the inspected sources neither establish nor disprove the alleged ministerial endorsement and publication without commissioning a substantive equity audit. The Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme reconstructs an automated route that contradicts uniform officer-confirmed processing. Colleen Taylor's testimony separately identifies her team's calculation-focused task; the Commission's own adverse finding concerning Online Compliance Intervention calculation and notification remains. Branch and task differences qualify the evidence for endorsement without establishing the absence of every formal duty. The earlier proposal provides a constructive comparison: cumulative evidence supports named knowledge findings and an instruction that advanced the proposal, while later failures to inquire and inform Cabinet remain. Such consequential participation is compatible with Utsho's concern about upstream authority, but does not itself establish deference or downstream reliance on a signature. The contribution is a source-specific explanation of what supports an endorsement claim and what documented participation leaves unresolved.

detail.abstract: Understanding how AI is reshaping work requires an accurate account of the tasks workers perform. Workers are often the first to see how their jobs are changing, as new responsibilities and tools often appear in everyday work before these changes reach formal descriptions. Interviews with workers can help capture these emerging changes in job tasks. Yet existing methods support standardized ratings across workers, while open-ended conversations with workers remain costly to collect and synthesize at scale. We introduce the Stanford Task Network (TaskNet), an occupational taxonomy grounded directly in workers' accounts of their everyday work. To construct TaskNet, we develop a mixed-initiative system that induces task inventories directly from workers. The system conducts interviews, standardizes reports into individual task lists, and aggregates these lists into occupational task inventories. Every statement is validated by 318 incumbents in 7923 ratings of relevance and importance. Relative to the task data from the O * NET 31.0 database for the sampled occupations, TaskNet covers 75% of the 118 published O * NET tasks and adds 79 tasks with no O * NET counterpart and 58 that refine existing statements. It covers 89 % of tasks reported by held-out workers, compared with 79 % for O * NET, and a larger share of the activities described in employer job postings (72.5% vs. 70.2%). TaskNet provides a foundation for keeping occupational information current and grounded in workers' experiences as AI reshapes work.

detail.abstract: Coastal regions in Asia and the Pacific concentrate economic activity while facing intensifying flood risk, yet who is most exposed—and how exposure relates to local wealth—remains poorly understood. Combining satellite-derived wealth estimates at 5 km and 500 m resolution with projected coastal inundation maps under multiple scenarios across 10 countries, we find that coastal areas are on average 0.75 standard deviations wealthier than inland areas—a broad based dividend spanning urban and rural communities. Within coastal zones, however, flood exposed populations are 0.26–0.39 standard deviations poorer than their neighbors. This aggregate masks sharp heterogeneity: Bangladesh, India, and Myanmar face a persistent double burden of deprivation and exposure while the wealth gap in Cambodia worsens under high emissions. In the Philippines, Timor-Leste, Indonesia, and Pakistan, exposure increasingly concentrates in wealthier areas. Climate risk and socioeconomic dynamics are thus intertwined in country-specific ways, reshaping who is most vulnerable as emissions rise.

detail.abstract: Canada's Competition Act was overhauled through Bills C-19 (2022), C-56 (2023) and C-59 (2024). This paper assesses those reforms against the market dynamics of algorithmic pricing and agentic AI. It finds real gains: the drip pricing prohibition and revenue-based penalties, recognition of network effects and non-price competition, repeal of the efficiencies defence, compulsory market studies, and expanded private access. It also identifies problems: statutory merger presumptions keyed to HHI thresholds calibrated for the US economy and blind to the non-price harms the Act now recognizes, a restructured abuse of dominance test that creates uncertainty, and a Bureau whose resources have not kept pace with its mandate. The central gap is that the Act is silent on algorithmic and agentic coordination. Section 45 requires an agreement, but autonomous agents can converge on supra-competitive prices without one, a risk sharpened by what Shahidi et al. call the Coasean Singularity. The paper proposes a presumption of agreement for shared pricing algorithms using non-public data, effects-based liability for autonomous convergence, algorithm disclosure and auditing, agent decision logging, interoperability obligations modelled on the Consumer-Driven Banking Act, a statutory duty of loyalty for consumer-facing agents, a Digital Markets Unit, and a regulatory markets model for oversight.

detail.abstract: We model the stock market as a damped spring and introduce two measures that investors can read like a price-earnings ratio. Resilience is the strength of the pull back to fair value, and the Stored Energy Index (SEI) measures how much rebound or correction potential the market has accumulated. In the model, value traders supply resilience and trend followers supply momentum, and the market can overshoot fair value only if trend followers are present. Using U.S. stock market data from 1901 to 2023 and a realtime measure of fair value, we find that the market glides back to fair value: half of a valuation gap closes in 5.7 years, with little overshooting. Momentum appears only above fair value. Below it, buying during the decline has paid as well as waiting for the turn. The SEI predicts real returns at one-to five-year horizons, and the forecast implied by the estimated spring beats the historical mean out of sample.

detail.abstract: Recent studies reveal a significant link between environmental pollution and diabetes. Оur study investigated the changes in some bioelements’ concentrations (Se, Fe, Cr and Mn) in the testis of adult diabetic rats with concomitant exposure to cadmium chloride (CdCl2). Diabetes was induced in newborn Wistar rats by a single i.p. injection of 100 mg/kg streptozotocin on postnatal day 1 alone or in combination of oral maternal Cd exposure at a daily dose of 5 mg/kg until postnatal day 25. Hyperglycemia was validated in all experimental groups on day 45 and 65. Testicular weight index was significantly reduced in Cd-exposed alone group and concomitant with diabetes on postnatal day 65. The analysis of five elements in the testicular homogenates by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) showed significantly increased Cd content in the Cd-exposed groups alone and in combination with diabetes which was more pronounced on day 45 compared to day 65, thus indicating metal clearance. The diabetic rats also significantly accumulated Cd. In all experimental groups Se content was elevated while Cr, Mn and Fe were reduced. In conclusion, our data show that exposure to Cd in early life is a diabetogenic factor with deteriorating effects on glucose profile in diabetic condition. This is associated with bioelements’ homeostasis leading to decreased relative testis weight in adulthood with possible impact on sperm quality. Moreover, our experimental model provides new data about possible role of maternal Cd administration in inducing metabolic reprogramming in the offspring.

detail.abstract: Introduction: Ibogaine is being studied for opioid use disorder (OUD), but a single episode adds long-term value only if early responses last. We compared a medically monitored ibogaine episode with protocolized medication for OUD (MOUD) rescue against starting buprenorphine or methadone.,Methods: We built a weekly cohort state-transition model of treatment-presenting, eligible U.S. adults over 10 years (health care sector perspective, 2024 US$, 3% discounting). The model tracks response, first return to use, MOUD status, opioid use and mortality. Without participant-level relapse data, durability was partially identified from one cohort's grouped follow-up under three curves, none a base case. Acquisition price was excluded; threshold prices are reported. One-way, structural and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were run, the latter sampling source uncertainty only, conditional on each curve and retention schedule.,Results: Versus buprenorphine, incremental QALYs per person were 0.0024, 0.0152 and 0.0125 under the fast-bound, Tier-1 upper-edge and proportional-transport curves, at $3,937 to $6,290 more before acquisition. ICERs were $2,673,000, $259,562 and $353,661 per QALY ($2,528,000, $217,217 and $307,945 versus methadone). Under a conservative mortality mapping the strategy caused 0.28 to 0.39 more deaths per 1,000; with background mortality after response it caused fewer, and Tier-1 ICERs were $86,535 and $75,705 per QALY. detail.abstract:
Background: Mental illnesses (MI) are a major disease burden, particularly among socioeconomically disadvantaged groups. In low and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Pakistan, mental health is underfunded, with only USD 2 per capita spent compared to USD 50 in high-income countries. Pakistan's MI burden is estimated at PKR 616.9 billion. 

Objective: This study estimates the cost of mental illness in Pakistan for 2023 and projects costs for 2030. Methods: Major mental illnesses were selected based on ICD-10 classification, with cost data gathered from previous studies. Costs were adjusted for 2023 using the GDP deflator, and future costs were projected considering inflation forecasts. 

Results and Discussion: A systematic review identified five relevant studies (two from India, three from Pakistan). Costs were analyzed for 12 disorders, with schizophrenia having the highest increase-from PKR 90,719 in 2006 to PKR 215,275 in 2023, projected to reach PKR 317,656 by 2030 (USD 1,147). Depression costs rose from PKR 133,296 in 2021 to PKR 176,557 in 2023, with a projected increase to PKR 286,837 by 2030 (USD 1,036). Costs for all disorders are expected to rise significantly, underscoring the urgent need for greater mental health investment in LMICs. 

Conclusion: With one-third of Pakistan's population below the poverty line, MI treatment is unaffordable, worsening financial burdens. This study highlights the need for increased mental health funding and cost-effective interventions to bridge the treatment gap.

detail.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate geographic disparities and vaccination effects on readmission and mortality among patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19 in Amazonas, Brazil. Study Design: Retrospective cohort study. Methods: We linked surveillance (SIVEP-Gripe) and mortality (SIM) databases from January 2020 to December 2022, including all hospitalized patients with severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS). Outcomes included time to severe COVID-19 readmission and death. Survival analyses and cure-fraction models assessed the effects of residence (capital vs. countryside) and vaccination period. Results: The cohort comprised 117,701 individuals. Incidence was consistently higher in the capital than in the countryside, peaking in 2021 (297.1 vs. 78.2 per 100,000). The post-vaccination period was associated with an approximately 83–84% reduction in the incidence of severe COVID-19 hospitalizations in both regions. Capital residents had a longer time to readmission, while countryside residents had a higher probability of cure. Survival probability was more than four times higher during the post-vaccination period. Conclusions: Vaccination has substantially reduced the incidence and improved survival, thereby mitigating pre-existing geographic disparities. Strengthening vaccination coverage and health system capacity remains essential to reduce regional inequalities.

Timor-Leste, a Southeast Asian nation with a high burden of acute lower respiratory infections, introduced Pneumosil (PCV-10, Serum Institute of India) into its national immunization program in January 2023, becoming the first country globally to do so. This case study analyzes the decision-making process, implementation strategies, and early outcomes using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) Methods: We conducted a descriptive case study applying the five CFIR domains (Intervention Characteristics, Inner Setting, Outer Setting, Individual Adopter Characteristics, and Implementation Process) to analyze the Pneumosil introduction process. Data sources included published literature, government documents, WHO guidelines, NITAG-TL meeting minutes, vaccine coverage data, and direct experience of authors involved in the decision-making process from 2018 to 2023. Results: The decision to introduce Pneumosil was informed by systematic evidence review including disease burden assessment, product comparison, and cost-effectiveness analysis. Implementation employed a Supplementary Immunization Activity (SIA) from January 12 to March 28, 2023, across all 13 municipalities. Overall coverage reached 74.0% (886/1,198 eligible children), ranging from 59.5% to 91.7% across municipalities. Key facilitators included WHO prequalification of Pneumosil, Ministry of Health leadership, international partnerships, and established cold chain infrastructure. Barriers included resource limitations, denominator data quality issues, and COVID-19-related delays. Conclusions: Timor-Leste's successful Pneumosil introduction demonstrates that with systematic planning, multi-stakeholder engagement, and attention to implementation science principles, resource-limited settings can introduce new vaccines. The 74% coverage achieved, though variable across municipalities, provides a foundation for routine immunization integration. Ongoing evaluation through WHO post-introduction protocols and research initiatives will assess long-term impact and inform future vaccine introductions.

detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Developing a medical image classifier requires choosing an architecture and training settings. detail.abstract: Clinical trials often show little average benefit while some patients clearly respond. Finding those patients in the trial's own data is usually dismissed as data dredging, while naming the subgroup in advance requires knowing the answer before the trial is run. We show that valid evidence survives an unrestricted search if, before outcomes are examined, investigators declare the form an acceptable answer may take: which measurements may be used, how many per rule, and which thresholds. In a conditional Gaussian benchmark, a certificate covering that declared language permits unrestricted adaptive search, with no penalty for how the final rule was found, and the patients it requires grow only with the logarithm of the number of admissible rules. A certificate protecting every patient subset instead retains a positive floor however large the trial grows, yet it also caps the price of any language, so small trials can search freely. We give a step-by-step procedure for corrected p-values and certified effect sizes, and in simulated trials of 50 to 800 patients, certification on the whole trial found the true subgroup more often than holdout designs at 200 to 400 patients, and about as often at 800. We then asked whether frontier language models can perform this search themselves, auditing chat-only configurations given synthetic trial tables. In 2,550 cases, a single-variable benefit at over five standard errors mostly drew no proposal, and forced four-variable answers named on average 0.27 of the four planted variables against 0.24 by chance. In 1,200 further cases across six configurations from two vendors, with a zero trial average, five configurations proposed a subgroup in 1.1% of attempts. The sixth recovered true variables well above chance, but its willingness to answer tracked effect size rather than whether the evidence could support a claim. Two failure modes emerge: silence uncorrelated with difficulty, and confidence only weakly tied to evidence. Both are addressed by a declared language with a calibrated certificate applied outside the model, and an abstention audit should report false claims, recovery and unusable output separately.

detail.abstract: Background: Gallbladder diseases exhibit substantial visual variability on ultrasound, while acoustic shadowing, irregular lesion morphology, and class imbalance complicate multiclass automated diagnosis. Conventional deep learning approaches may not adequately accommodate irregular spatial structures or preserve boundary-related information. This study proposes Ada-TransGBC, a lightweight framework for five-class gallbladder ultrasound classification.,Methods: Ada-TransGBC combines an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 backbone with Adaptive Deformable Strip Attention (ADSA), Shadow-Aware Gated Attention (SAGA), and an Edge-Guided Boundary-Aware Auxiliary Loss (EGBAL) branch. ADSA models irregular directional structures, SAGA modulates spatial feature responses in potentially shadow-affected regions, and EGBAL promotes boundary-sensitive representation learning using Canny-derived pseudo-boundaries. Class imbalance was addressed using soft class-balanced sampling and focal loss with label smoothing. MixUp, progressive backbone unfreezing, discriminative learning rates, and test-time augmentation were also employed. The framework was evaluated across abnormal, benign/mass-type, malignant, normal, and stone categories.,Results: Ada-TransGBC achieved 81.57% accuracy, with macro-precision, macro-recall, and macro-F1 scores of 77.68%, 80.03%, and 78.40%, respectively, and a weighted-F1 score of 81.93%. The macro-ROC-AUC was 0.957, with class-specific AUCs ranging from 0.911 to 0.988. The normal class achieved the highest F1-score (87.91%), whereas benign/mass-type lesions were the most challenging (66.12%). Its performance exceeded that of the EfficientNet-B0 baseline under the evaluated experimental conditions, while the ablation results supported the value of the combined configuration. detail.abstract:
Every protection ordinary people have held against concentrated power rests on the powerful needing them. Mass protest succeeds partly because security forces may refuse to act against citizens. War is restrained partly because citizens must fight and pay for it. Nations are held together partly by shared work, schooling, service and taxes. This book asks what happens to each of these protections as artificial intelligence and robotics reduce the human labour that force, defence and production require.

It builds on a task-based model of labour necessity (Kano 2026) and applies it to enforcement. Refusal leverage, the share of an operation that would stop if its staff refused, falls with the automation frontier rather than with actual deployment. It therefore declines years before employment does, and headcount understates the loss. In the central case leverage falls below one half in year 13 after the threshold, when 63 per cent of staff are still employed, and the lead ranges from 0 to 15 years across 27 cases. Linked to the NAVCO 1.2 data on 389 campaigns, this implies that the success rate of large nonviolent campaigns could fall from about 57 to about 36 per cent.

Further models cover the cost-exchange ratio between cheap drones and interceptors, escalation between automated defences, how the severity of attacks changes when fewer people are needed to carry them out, and frontier rents on the Moon and the deep seabed. An integrated model follows one technological shock through three stylised nations. They diverge when machines can perform about half of enforcement tasks, and the difference is wholly institutional. Institutions whose strength depends on the leverage of those still needed erode as necessity falls. Those entrenched early, or based on claims independent of necessity such as shared ownership and citizenship, persist.

The book proposes a Human Veto over the use of force by machines. It measures the lag between technology and the rules that govern it, which it calls the Rule Gap, and sets out warning signs and falsifiable predictions.

detail.abstract: Retirement readiness has been conceptualized and measured inconsistently, limiting comparisons across studies and reducing the applicability of existing instruments in diverse educational contexts. This study reports the initial development and validation of the Retirement Readiness Strain Scale (RRSS), a brief instrument derived from a broader pool of retirement-readiness items administered to Pakistani public school teachers. Using survey data from 179 participants, principal component analysis reduced the original 22-item pool to eight retained items, which were subsequently evaluated using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. The retained items, reflecting occupational stress, work-family conflict, and workload demands, demonstrated a coherent one-factor structure, good internal consistency, and expected relationships with theoretically related and distinct constructs. Research findings suggest that strain emerged as a salient dimension of perceived retirement readiness within the educational context of Pakistan public school system and did not entirely replace the multidimensional measures of retirement readiness. The RRSS offers an initial measure of this empirically derived dimension and provides educational researchers with a brief instrument to examine teacher workforce sustainability and retirement-related perceptions in underrepresented educational settings. This study contributes to a more contextually grounded understanding of teacher workforce sustainability and demonstrates the value of developing and validating educational measures in the settings where they are intended to be used. Education authorities and public managers can use the RRSS as a lowburden tool to monitor workforce strain and inform workload, retention and pension policy.

detail.abstract: This paper tests whether borrower age predicts selection into payment-minimizing mortgage features controlling for the mobility and income-growth channels that the standard life-cycle model (Campbell & Cocco, 2003) says should explain the selection instead. Using 2021, 2023, and 2024 HMDA data on home-purchase loans nationwide, I model four such features (adjustable-rate, interest-only, extended-term, and balloon) and find that a single federal rule (the Dodd-Frank Qualified Mortgage rule) has made all but adjustable-rate(ARM) loans rare nearly everywhere. In the high-rate years (2023-2024), ARM is the dominant feature in all 51 states/DC; in the low-rate year 2021, ARM dominates in only 43, with interest-only dominant in the other 8-showing that uniform ARM dominance is a feature of the rate environment. Controlling for mobility, income growth, loan size, loan program, lender identity, and state fixed effects, a residual age effect survives, but runs opposite to the hypothesis. Instead of younger buyers with limited credit choosing lower payments, the effect is strongest among older borrowers who have more financial flexibility, especially those with balloon payments. This finding consistently appears in all three years and under both interest rate conditions. In contrast, the pattern among borrowers under 35 varies depending on interest rate conditions and is not consistent across the years. These results suggest that affordability is not the main reason borrowers choose these loans. Instead, there are possible explanations that remain: older borrowers may have reasons for wanting shorter loan terms, there may be an unobserved short-tenure motive among older borrowers, or older borrowers may be less concerned about payment risks because they have more financial resources to fall back on.

detail.abstract: We study a canonical heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian (HANK) economy populated by LLM-driven households, a heterogeneous population whose consumption rules are generated by a large language model (LLM) rather than derived from optimization. We measure their consumption, saving, and expectations with designs from experimental economics. Summarized by the household's intertemporal marginal propensities to consume, the measured behavior closes the economy in general equilibrium and yields fiscal and monetary multipliers alongside the rational-expectations benchmark. The main lesson is methodological. For an LLM-driven household, how expectations are measured is part of the model. Announcing a future income change for each horizon separately leads the household to weigh the size of the change but not its timing, so that it appears myopic, whereas presenting the horizons together draws out the response to timing. In equilibrium, under joint evaluation, LLM-driven households anticipate announced policy yet overweight the near horizon relative to rational expectations, raising the fiscal multiplier above the myopic benchmark and above the constructed rational one. Both findings hold for each of three LLMs from different model families, with the size of the over-reaction varying across them. In the main experiments, removing the instruction that asks the household to weigh the timing of an announced change roughly halves the measured over-reaction and leaves the ordering of the multipliers unchanged.

detail.abstract: Empirical work on product market competition typically summarizes a firm's environment in a single number, such as an industry concentration ratio or a measure of competitive pressure. Evidence from production networks shows that such summaries can discard structure that matters, and I ask whether the same holds among competitors. The text-based ecosystem of Hoberg and Phillips (2016) makes the question answerable, because its pairwise and firm-level measures are all built from the same 10-K product descriptions and are therefore comparable on equal terms. Shocks transmit between product market rivals, but transmission does not vary with how similar two firms' products are, with the crowding of a firm's neighborhood, with the speed at which it changes its products, or with the congruence of two firms' life cycles. It varies instead with pairwise vertical relatedness. No configuration of these measures forecasts cash flow out of sample better than a concentration index computed from the same network. What travels between two firms follows the economic connection between them rather than the resemblance of their products, and measuring that resemblance more finely does not help.

detail.abstract: Visual tokenization provides a fundamental interface between continuous image data and modern Vision and Multimodal Foundation Models. Existing approaches typically rely on uniform patchification, which can cause high-frequency spatial aliasing and increase computational costs. Others use neural codebooks, but these can lead to codebook collapse, unstable training, and loss of structural information. To address these issues, we present Directional Spatial-Graph Byte Pair Encoding (SG-BPE). This method is deterministic and non-neural. It adapts Byte Pair Encoding for visual data by turning images into planar graphs of atomic patches and merging adjacent nodes step by step along horizontal and vertical directions. We establish four theoretical guarantees: (1) the Axis-Aligned Rectangular Closure Theorem, ensuring all visual morphemes remain rectangular; (2) the Conditional Dirichlet Energy Dissipation Theorem, establishing monotonic energy dissipation under balanced gradient boundaries and deriving contrast bounds for transverse interface residuals; (3) the Structural Bijectivity Theorem, proving zero structural information loss (LBPE = 0); and (4) a Helmholtz Free Energy Minimization Framework linking spatial BPE to statistical thermodynamics under the Minimum Description Length principle. We integrate SG-BPE with Transformer architectures using Scale-Aware 2D Rotary Position Embeddings, an inversescale density attention prior, Visual BPE-Dropout for topological data augmentation, and Information-Theoretic Halting for adaptive sequence lengths. We further extend the framework to Spatio-Temporal 3D-BPE and establish a Temporal Closure Theorem for space-time tube representations. Experiments on the Oxford-IIIT Pet corpus (7,349 unique scenes from 7,390 images; 7.53 × 10 6 patches) demonstrate 44.1% sequence-length compression at vocabulary size |V| = 2048, reducing sequences to 572.9±78.6 tokens and achieving a 3.19× theoretical attention FLOP reduction and 1.60× measured forward speedup on a Tesla T4 GPU. In high-compression settings, self-attention latency improves by up to 5.49×, with a 5.18× theoretical FLOP reduction at N = 450. At |V| = 1024, compression reaches 36.54%, with a 2.48× theoretical FLOP reduction. Reconstruction achieves PSNR values of 27.80 ± 1.96 dB and 27.26 dB at vocabulary sizes of 2048 and 1024, respectively, without learned neural weights. Thermodynamic ablations show a 36.6% reduction in empirical Dirichlet energy under simulated annealing at |V| = 1024 (31.41 → 19.90 J/image), while the larger vocabulary exhibits near-asymptotic convergence. SG-BPE also maintains at least 96.1% boundary-partition stability (Jaccard IoU) under sensor noise (σ ≤ 0.15). Overall, SG-BPE offers a theoretically grounded, parameter-free approach to visual tokenization, providing a promising foundation for scalable vision and multimodal architectures.

detail.abstract: Many studies use difference-in-differences (DiD) estimators to study how carbon pricing affects stock returns. However, few studies have asked how much their results depend on the parallel-trends assumption that makes the results possible. This paper examines this question using the reform of the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) Market Stability Reserve in 2018, which doubled the rate at which surplus allowances are withheld from the market. We use monthly risk-adjusted returns from eight iShares STOXX Europe 600 sector UCITS ETFs. We find a positive and statistically significant average effect using the wild-cluster bootstrap (p = 0.0078). This significance depends on the estimator. This result is not significant when we use Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, which allow the sectors to be correlated. We then use two additional tests that the literature does not usually do. First, we compute the breakdown value of Rambachan and Roth (2023), which says how large a violation of the parallel trend assumption the result can tolerate before its sign is no longer identified. We find a breakdown value of zero; the identified set contains zero even before violation of the assumption. Second, we compute the minimum detectable effect the design could reliably detect. It is 6.80% per year, which is greater than our estimated effect of 4.95% per year. The design therefore has only about 50% power to find the effect it computes. These two results explain each other. The design is not detecting a fragile true effect. A separate double machine learning analysis of allowance-price pass-through is not statistically distinguishable from zero. But the interval is too wide to say that pass-through is not economically meaningful. Our conclusion is about methods rather than carbon pricing. Results do not show that carbon pricing has no effect on European stock market returns, but the estimated effect from this sector-level DiD design is sensitive to the assumption it makes. With few sectors and noisy returns, significance can rest on the parallel-trends assumption, on pooling many periods, and on treating sectors as independent, rather than on a robustly identified effect. Breakdown values and power calculations show that this dependence is visible, and we suggest that such methods should be routinely reported in similar empirical studies. The Commission's July 2026 proposal would return the same intake rate to 12% from 2028, three years earlier than existing law, partly reversing the event we study. A natural next study is to use the same tests for both events, using firm-level data instead of sector-level data.

detail.abstract: The public cannot fully observe what the U.S. president is working on, and the president chooses what to communicate publicly. I examine what drives this strategic disclosure choice and its capital-market implications. Using Presidential Daily Diaries, I reconstruct the president’s minute-by-minute schedule from 1935 through 2009. I use an LLM-assisted process to identify the potential policy topics discussed in each presidential meeting and use the same process to identify the topics in the president’s public communications. I then measure the similarity between potential meeting topics and presidential public communications. I find evidence that suggests presidential public communications more closely reflect what the President is working on when the issues are important to voters and less closely when they are politically divisive. Specifically, presidents communicate relatively less about issues that divide their own party but relatively more about issues that divide the two parties. Greater similarity between potential meeting topics and presidential public communications is associated with lower subsequent market uncertainty at both the aggregate and firm levels. Additional analyses suggest that when presidential approval is relatively low, presidents communicate more about voter priorities and less about within-party divisions. Presidential public communications also more closely reflect what the President is working on near Election Day when the incumbent seeks reelection and around funding deadlines that could produce a government shutdown. The negative association between similarity and uncertainty is stronger among firms with greater exposure to government demand and weaker among firms that meet with the president. Together, these findings are consistent with presidents weighing political benefits and costs when choosing what to communicate publicly, as suggested by voluntary disclosure theory, and with presidential public communications having capital-market implications.

detail.abstract:
Canada's courts are open to everyone, in the way an old remark said the Ritz Hotel is open to everyone: the door is open, but few can afford to walk in. Almost half of Canadian adults face a serious civil or family legal problem over any three years, yet about one in five obtains legal advice and fewer than one in ten reaches a court or tribunal. In Ontario a civil case can take four to five years to reach trial; more than half of the parties in family cases file without a lawyer; and the Landlord and Tenant Board's active caseload has stood at about three times its pre-pandemic level. Many Canadians believe the system is designed so that lawyers get rich. This paper tests that belief.

It begins with what the system promised. From Magna Carta's pledge not to sell, deny or delay justice, through the rule of law in the Charter and the Supreme Court's decisions in Trial Lawyers Association, Hryniak and Pintea, to Canada's international commitments, the promise is that justice will be reachable, timely, understandable, equal and respectful of the dignity of the person. The paper measures the system against those five parts and finds that it falls short on all of them. The failure is not at the bench, where cases that arrive are decided fairly, but on the road to it.

Testing the popular belief, the paper finds it wrong about motive and right about effect. No one designed the system to enrich lawyers, and most lawyers are not rich. But the system is built and run almost entirely by insiders: judges and lawyers write the rules, with no public member on either of Ontario's rules committees; lawyers govern the body that decides who may compete with them; and hourly billing rewards every added step. The people who use the courts pay for every lever and hold none. Applying the four checks of Channels, Not Dams, the paper finds that the system checks its members for misconduct but does not check itself for whether it keeps its promise.

It proposes three things: an Access to Justice Act that makes timely civil and family justice a right, with published time standards and consequences that fall on the system rather than the parties; an independent Justice Access Office, reporting to the Legislature, with a third of the seats on the rules committees for members of the public and written answers required within 45 days; and targeted repairs. Four invented people, each labelled, carry the story from the inside.

detail.abstract: We study a geometric diagnostic of distributional heterogeneity across periods of riskadjusted returns. SEBI's studies report about Rs 3.85 lakh crore of individual traders' net losses in Indian equity derivatives between FY22 and FY26. Participation fell after the measures introduced from October 2024, but 87.7 percent of individuals in the FY26 broker sample lost money. This paper examines what the regulatory record and aggregate exchange data can establish about costs, counterparties, positioning, trading hours and signal provenance.

The paper is Part 2 of the Signal Provenance series. Part 1 identified the missing link between a signal and the resulting order. This paper considers that gap alongside retail investor protection. It distinguishes access restrictions from surveillance and settlement reforms, including SEBI's existing responsibility rule for AI use. Contested interim orders concerning index trading and closing auctions illustrate specific alleged mechanisms; they are not treated as final findings or explanations of all retail losses.

NSE participant data shows a reversal in index-futures positioning: the Client category's October 2026 average long share was about 84 percent, compared with 9 percent for FII. Client is not a verified proxy for individuals. From 21 August to 22 October 2026, foreign investors sold a net Rs 1,06,956 crore in cash equities while domestic institutions bought Rs 1,57,928 crore and NIFTY fell 6.45 percent. A futures-only mark-to-market approximation cannot identify household losses or total portfolio returns. In a separate 19-expiry reconstruction using explicit exchange expiry identifiers, max pain was closer to the expiry-day underlying close than the previous close in 12 cases, but median misses were larger in three of four groups. This small selected sample establishes no robust forecasting advantage or manipulation mechanism.

Four proposals address information at the point of trade. A provenance category carried with the order would record a reported source category without message content. A pilot should test completeness, reliability and privacy before any mandate. The paper does not claim that provenance reduces losses or that the observed associations identify their causes.

detail.abstract: We consider the following variant of the Monty Hall Problem. There are n doors, behind each of which hides an a priori random reward, independently distributed according to a common prior. A clue box is attached to each door, which, if inspected, yields a clue about the rewards behind possibly all doors. The game host designs what clues to be put in each box and announces at the beginning of the game what each clue reveals about the rewards. Given the design, the player decides sequentially which clue box to inspect by paying an inspection fee and when to stop inspecting the boxes. Upon stopping, the player can then utilize the clues collected so far to open a door whose attached box has already been inspected and take the reward behind it. The player wishes to maximize the reward obtained from the opened door, while the host maximizes the fees collected from inspections. Under specific designs, the player's problem can be reduced to several classic sequential information acquisition problems, such as the Pandora's box problem or the Wald's sequential sampling problem. We study the optimal designs of the clue boxes when the host faces different informational constraints. These informational constraints arise from the potential applications in different settings such as product-page design on online platforms, information design in delegated search, and reward design in video games.

detail.abstract: We study online conformal prediction in a partially observed panel: a new cross-section of peer outcomes is observed before each target outcome, target feedback may be intermittent or absent, and neither units nor rounds need be exchangeable. We propose Weighted Temporal Quantile Adjustment (W-TQA), which combines similarity weights learned from unit histories with an adaptive target-specific miscoverage level. We prove that neither target-peer mismatch nor coverage on unrevealed rounds is identifiable, so assumptions on crossunit similarity and on the feedback mechanism cannot be avoided. We bound the past-conditional miscoverage in terms of this mismatch, quantify the cost of learning the weights under a profile-similarity assumption, and show that the implemented procedure, which falls back on the largest peer score, attains long-run average coverage under missing-completely-at-random feedback and a feasibility condition on the calibration panel. On synthetic panels and four real panels, including a genuinely asynchronous U.S.-to-Tokyo equity panel, W-TQA attains the highest coverage on the worst-covered target units on every panel; similarity weighting contributes most when target feedback is scarce, and temporal adaptation more as feedback accumulates.

detail.abstract:
On April 21, 2026, Japan’s air traffic control (ATC) system suffered a catastrophic 5-hour-and-15-minute outage, resulting in 269 flight cancellations and 607 delays among domestic carriers alone. While the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) initially reported a degradation of ATC processing capacity at the Kobe Area Control Center (ACC) triggered by a failure at the Fukuoka ACC, its final investigation report on July 28, 2026, entirely omitted any reference to the Kobe ACC. Instead, MLIT framed the incident as an isolated overload within a single component—the Flight Object Administration Center System (FACE)—caused by unattributed “processing requests”.

Relying exclusively on open-source intelligence (OSINT)—including official MLIT system architecture schematics, procurement records, press releases, and standard air traffic management (ATM) engineering literature—this paper conducts a socio-technical and institutional anatomy of the 2026 outage. First, by contrasting Japan’s architecture with the United States Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) decentralized En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) framework, we expose a critical “Two-Core, Three-HMI” architectural asymmetry. Although MLIT completed a drastic airspace reorganization in March 2025 that divided domestic airspace across three ACCs (Tokyo, Kobe, and Fukuoka), the Trajectorized En-route Traffic Data Processing System (TEPS) retains central processing systems in only two bases (Tokyo and Fukuoka), leaving the Kobe ACC as a “headless” node equipped solely with a Human-Machine Interface (HMI) processing system. Furthermore, FACE’s Flight Object Database (FODB) is tightly coupled via bidirectional update and distribution channels with downstream trajectory and traffic management systems (TEPS, ICAP, and TEAM). Second, we demonstrate how this technical tight coupling is exacerbated by fragmented procurement: all 11 annual maintenance and operational support contracts (totaling JPY 4.60 billion) were awarded on April 1, 2026—just 20 days before the outage—through competitive tenders (comprehensive evaluation method) each of which attracted a single bidder, split across three locked-in vendors (NEC, NTT Data, and Mitsubishi Electric). Third, we analyze MLIT’s post-incident reporting through the lens of bureaucratic blame avoidance, showing how erasing the Kobe ACC and black-boxing inter-system interfaces obscured both the structural vulnerability of the 2025 airspace reorganization and the blurred contractual liability boundaries among incumbent vendors—creating acute statutory risks regarding double fiscal expenditure and corporate tax cost attribution. To resolve this structural vulnerability, we propose a concrete architectural reform: deploying dedicated central processing servers at the Kobe ACC to establish a symmetric, one-to-one alignment between processing cores and HMI consoles across an East (Tokyo), Central (Kobe), and West (Fukuoka) “Tri-Core” topology, thereby eliminating the processing–display twist and dramatically enhancing national fault tolerance.

detail.abstract:
The United States combines high income and human development with substantial inequality, comparatively weak perceived governmental care, and the highest reported discrimination in the available 53-country survey sample. This paper examines that configuration through the Economics of Belonging, distinguishing growth, stability, distribution, human capabilities, and social and institutional belonging. Using an audited 55-country database, it compares the United States with seven European economies, Canada and Mexico, and Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and China.


The analysis separates reported discrimination from a statistical adjustment for relative income and freedom of expression. In an equally weighted country-level model with 53 observations, freedom of expression is positively associated with discrimination reporting, whereas the income coefficient is imprecisely estimated after expression is included. At common reference conditions, the US reported value of 50.52% corresponds to a standardized score of 45.08. Substantial gaps remain relative to the selected European countries, Canada, Mexico, Japan, and South Korea. The US–China gap falls from 26.32 to 5.83 percentage points under the linear adjustment but reverses under a bounded nonlinear sensitivity analysis.


The results do not support interpreting reported discrimination as a direct ranking of underlying discriminatory treatment or treating adjustment as recovery of a true incidence rate. The American profile illustrates how economic resources, interpersonal care, institutional access, and perceived recognition can diverge. The paper develops a research agenda for inclusive participation that preserves expressive freedom and the capacity to report exclusion.


The main data used in this study are available in the replication package accompanying The Economics of Belonging: Measuring Economic and Social Achievement across Nations (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23603825). A supplementary archive, United_States_Belonging_Replication.zip (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23674517), provides the analysis files and code needed to reproduce the calculations reported in this article.

detail.abstract: Governments adopt digital procurement systems to curb misconduct, and anomaly detection offers a cheap way to check whether they work. A falling anomaly rate, however, can reflect better record-keeping as much as better behavior. This paper asks what moved when the share of flagged contracts in Kenya fell after two reforms in 2024, a digitization upgrade of the procurement portal and a capacity-building levy. I use contract-level data from Kenya’s Public Procurement Regulatory Authority for January 2024 to June 2025 and estimate the changes with interrupted time-series regression, since no untreated comparison group exists. The flagged share dropped from about 46% to about 9%. One flag accounts for most of the fall: contracts with no supplier record went from about 43% of contracts to under 1%. Flags unrelated to supplier records did not fall. On this evidence I read the drop as an improvement in record quality and find no evidence that other irregularities declined. The paper also offers a reproducible template for auditing audit metrics where data are scarce.
